caption_used: Number of participants (N=6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial. The horizontal bar chart displays seven criteria ranked by participant endorsement. Relevant FCs was unanimously selected by all 6 participants, followed by FC Summary at 5. Relevance Explanation and Clarity and Simplicity each received 3 endorsements. Overall Summary was highlighted by 2 participants, while Filters and Veracity Explanation each received 1. Notably, the top three criteria — Relevant FCs, FC Summary, and Relevance Explanation — together account for approximately 82% of all endorsements, indicating a strong consensus around content retrieval and summarization features over interface and transparency elements such as Filters and Veracity Explanation.
raw_response:
This horizontal bar chart illustrates the number of participants (N=6) who identified each of seven evaluation criteria as beneficial, with the criteria ranked in descending order of endorsement along the vertical axis labeled “Criterion” and the horizontal axis labeled “Number of Participants” ranging from 0 to 6 in increments of 2. The bars, each uniquely colored and labeled with its corresponding criterion and exact count, show that “Relevant FCs” (dark purple) received the highest endorsement at 6 participants, followed by “FC Summary” (dark blue) at 5, “Relevance Explanation” (teal) and “Clarity and Simplicity” (greenish-teal) each at 3, “Overall Summary” (light green) at 2, and both “Filters” (lighter green) and “Veracity Explanation” (yellow-green) at 1. The bars are sorted from top to bottom in descending order of participant count, visually emphasizing the top-ranked criteria. No additional annotations, error bars, or shading are present beyond the color-coded bars and their numerical labels.
